title: Casper and the Thorn
premise: Kestrel Ashgrove's ledgers record the Thorn Guild's trades in impossible things—years, names, favors owed to the dead. When a feral child arrives speaking the First Tongue, Kestrel realizes the guild has been quietly selling pieces of King Aldric's soul for a decade, and the thing wearing his crown is nearly whole. Bound by debt she cannot pay and loyalty to the mentor who sold her, Kestrel must choose between exposing the guild and saving a kingdom that never noticed her. In the end she burns the ledgers, unbinds the king with the child's forgotten language, and accepts exile—only to find the child, now hers in every way that matters, chooses to follow.
about_author: Coral Blackwood spent seven years cataloguing rare manuscripts in a private collection before turning to fiction, a period that seeded her obsession with documents that outlive their keepers. She writes from a coastal town where the fog arrives on schedule, and claims her best ideas come from marginalia left by strangers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet her in the Thorn Guild's counting room, invisible among scribes, balancing entries for traded years and borrowed luck. Her mentor Veyra reminds her of the debt that owns her. A knock at the guild door after closing: a mud-streaked child who speaks no known language. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine—the sense that order is a thin skin over something hungry.

chapters.title: A Language Older Than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The child, whom she names Casper, sleeps in the ledger vault; his sleep-talk matches glyphs in the guild's oldest sealed volume—a text even Veyra won't touch. Kestrel secretly copies pages, discovering references to a king 'hollowed by installments.' Emotional beat: wonder curdling into fear as she realizes the guild isn't just trading impossibilities—it's manufacturing them.

chapters.title: What the Crown Pays For
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Kestrel at the guild, then a courtier's desperate midnight visit selling 'one memory of the king's coronation.' Kestrel follows the ledger trail: ten years of purchases, all signed with the royal seal, all buying back pieces of Aldric himself. Emotional beat: vertigo—her small honest work has been bookkeeping for a slow regicide.

chapters.title: Veyra's Kindness
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Veyra discovers Kestrel's copied pages—and instead of punishing her, offers freedom: erase the evidence, forget Casper, and her debt dissolves. Flashbacks reveal Veyra bought Kestrel as a child too, raised her as both daughter and collateral. Emotional beat: love weaponized; Kestrel realizes every kindness was an entry in a ledger.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court
chapters.summary: Casper's POV (rendered through Kestrel's translation). Disguised as an auditor's clerk, Kestrel brings Casper to the palace, where King Aldric receives them with unsettling warmth—he recognizes Casper's language because he dreamed it before the crown took him. The queen begs Kestrel privately: the king weeps at nothing and remembers less each week. Emotional beat: tenderness inside decay; duty and love beginning to pull apart.

chapters.title: Entries in Red Ink
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She finds the master ledger: the buyer of the king's soul-pieces is the guild itself, feeding them to something bound beneath the counting room floor—an entity called the Thorn, which Veyra serves to keep her own name out of any ledger. Casper's language is the binding script. Emotional beat: betrayal compounded; the truth costs more than ignorance ever did.

chapters.title: The Price of Staying Invisible
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Veyra gives an ultimatum: hand over Casper or be entered into the ledger herself—owned, body and will, forever. Kestrel flees with the boy through the guild's flooded underlevels while the Thorn whispers her debts aloud, tempting her with surrender. Emotional beat: terror and clarity; invisibility was always just another form of being owned.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Palace chapel, night. Kestrel's POV. Using Casper as living key and the First Tongue as blade, she begins unbinding the king—but the ritual requires a debt freely forgiven, and the only soul entangled with hers enough to forgive is Veyra, arriving with guards. Kestrel confesses everything: resentment, love, the truth of what Veyra saved her from and sold her into. Emotional beat: the climax's hinge—truth offered as the only currency left.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burns
chapters.summary: Dual POV climax. Veyra, undone not by force but by forgiveness, speaks the release; the Thorn, starved of its contracts, tears free of the king and collapses into ash as Kestrel feeds it the burning ledgers. Aldric wakes hollow but human; Casper's language fades from him as its purpose ends. Emotional beat: catharsis through sacrifice—every debt cancelled at once, including Kestrel's.

chapters.title: Marginalia
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, one year later. Exiled from the capital, she keeps a small shop mending old books. Veyra sends no letters, only blank pages—a peace offering. A traveler brings a manuscript in the First Tongue; Casper, growing, translates a little, laughing. The last line mirrors the first ledger entry, rewritten: 'Received: one child. Owed: everything. Paid in full.' Emotional beat: earned quiet—love chosen over duty, truth kept over safety.
